### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. short-rib thoracic dysplasia 7 with or without polydactyly  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.787)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:29250)

**Proposed mechanism:** WDR35 (HGNC:29250) —DISRUPTS→ Ciliary protein trafficking and function (GO:0098550); Ciliary protein trafficking and function (GO:0098550) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal dysplasia (HP:0002650); Ciliary protein trafficking and function (GO:0098550) —LEADS_TO→ Thoracic dysplasia (HP:0006379); Ciliary protein trafficking and function (GO:0098550) —LEADS_TO→ Ectodermal dysplasia (HP:0000964); Ciliary protein trafficking and function (GO:0098550) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249). Loss-of-function mutations in WDR35 disrupt ciliary protein trafficking and function, leading to a spectrum of phenotypes including skeletal dysplasia, thoracic dysplasia, ectodermal dysplasia, and intellectual disability, consistent with both short-rib thoracic dysplasia 7 and skeletal dysplasia, ectodermal dysplasia, and intellectual disability syndrome.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of individuals with pathogenic WDR35 variants who do not exhibit any features of skeletal dysplasia, thoracic dysplasia, ectodermal dysplasia, or intellectual disability would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: Exome Variant Server (EVS) or gnomAD data showing a pathogenic allele frequency > 0.1% for WDR35 variants associated with these diseases.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the role of WDR35 in ciliary function provides a common therapeutic target for both short-rib thoracic dysplasia 7 and skeletal dysplasia, ectodermal dysplasia, and intellectual disability syndrome, potentially leading to novel treatment strategies aimed at restoring ciliary function or mitigating downstream cellular defects.

#### 2. cranioectodermal dysplasia 1  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.486)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5620924, Reactome:R-HSA-5610787)

**Proposed mechanism:** WDR35 (HGNC:24262) —DISRUPTS→ Intraflagellar Transport (IFT) complex assembly and function (GO:0031252); IFT122 (HGNC:20803) —DISRUPTS→ Intraflagellar Transport (IFT) complex assembly and function (GO:0031252); Intraflagellar Transport (IFT) complex assembly and function (GO:0031252) —DISRUPTS→ Ciliary signaling and development (GO:0007427); Ciliary signaling and development (GO:0007427) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal abnormalities (HP:0000924); Ciliary signaling and development (GO:0007427) —LEADS_TO→ Craniofacial abnormalities (HP:0000278); Ciliary signaling and development (GO:0007427) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal hair morphology (HP:0001083); Ciliary signaling and development (GO:0007427) —LEADS_TO→ Short stature (HP:0004305). Loss-of-function mutations in WDR35 and IFT122 disrupt the assembly and function of the Intraflagellar Transport (IFT) machinery. This impairment leads to defective ciliary signaling and development, ultimately manifesting as overlapping phenotypes such as skeletal abnormalities, craniofacial abnormalities, abnormal hair morphology, and short stature in both MONDO:0013323 and cranioectodermal dysplasia 1.

**How to falsify it:** If genetic analysis reveals that the causal variants for MONDO:0013323 and cranioectodermal dysplasia 1 are in genes completely unrelated to ciliary function or intraflagellar transport, and these genes do not converge on any shared downstream pathways or processes, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: Discovery of a common, high-frequency (e.g., >1% in gnomAD) loss-of-function variant in either WDR35 or IFT122 that is strongly associated with only one of the diseases, while the other disease is caused by a distinct mechanism.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism of ciliary protein trafficking defects in MONDO:0013323 and cranioectodermal dysplasia 1 could lead to the identification of common therapeutic targets. Modulating the intraflagellar transport pathway or downstream signaling cascades affected by ciliary dysfunction may offer a unified therapeutic strategy for patients with these related rare diseases.

This dysfunction in ciliary biology underlies the shared skeletal and thoracic abnormalities observed in both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in IFT52 in human populations (e.g., gnomAD) do not segregate with either disease, or that the identified mutations in IFT52 do not impair ciliary function in experimental models. _(variant: Exome allele frequency > 0.01 for pathogenic variants in IFT52)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of IFT52 and primary cilia dysfunction in these distinct skeletal dysplasias could lead to the identification of common therapeutic targets for improving skeletal development and reducing thoracic insufficiency.
